meta.method: Pass 1: news-first sweep of wet-season months (Apr–Nov) using Task 26 outlets and qualifying rule. Pass 2: recall via wires/aggregators, death and dam queries, official sites, plus a once-per-year out-of-season check (Jan–Mar, Dec). Qualifying reports name a Lagos State place and a date, and describe water on streets or in homes. Quotes ≤25 words, verbatim. Dates, numbers and quotes are only those in the source. Areas left as named; not geocoded. Flood date is the flood day, not publication day.
notes: Generic date-range search leaked 2025–2026 stories; 2024 kept only from year-in-URL hits or a readable published_at in 2024.
Premium Times, Guardian NG, Daily Trust and TVC: no qualifying 2024 Lagos street/home flood with a named date found (alerts, enforcement, opinion, or other-year leaks).
X accounts of LASEMA, Lagos MoE and NEMA: no dated 2024 flood posts reached.
Anadolu, Reuters, AFP, Al Jazeera and Xinhua 2024 Nigeria flood copy was national (Jigawa, Maiduguri) not a named Lagos flood day.
Oyan Dam 2024 hits were warnings or monitoring, not observed Lagos flooding.
ReliefWeb/IOM-NEMA-LASEMA DTM Lagos post-flood report (30 Dec 2024) is a seasonal aggregate (14 LGAs; 275,621 affected), not a dated flood day — logged excluded.
Dartmouth Flood Observatory: no Lagos-matched 2024 event list reached.
Punch 7 Jul feature mislabels Wednesday as 4 Jul 2024 (Wednesday was 3 Jul); kept as the 3 Jul flood, matching same-day outlets.
Feb 20 Alimosho flood kept from the out-of-season check. NEMA also mentioned a similar Sunday event (18 Feb) without named places — not kept as a separate report.

reports.impacts: Flooding in Agungi and environs after 48 hours of continuous rainfall. Emergency Flood Abatement Gang deployed while rain was ongoing to clear debris in collectors. Minor encroachment and a blockage found along Alfa Beach behind James Hope University.
reports.quote: the flooding incidents experienced as a result of the 48 hours of continuous rainfall experienced in the state
reports.cause_quote: the collector they have there is too small to serve the volume of storm water on the Agungi stretch
reports.cause_who: Tokunbo Wahab, Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources

reports.impacts: Heavy rain from early Wednesday flooded many parts of Lagos; commuters stranded. Iyana-Oworo/Olopo Meji toward Third Mainland Bridge completely flooded, traffic to Alapere. Tree fell at Airport U-turn, Oshodi; LASTMA cleared it. Wahab said the Olopomeji section was later free of rainwater.
reports.quote: A heavy rainfall early Wednesday morning has flooded many parts of Lagos, making it difficult for commuters to move to their destinations.
reports.cause_quote: A heavy rainfall early Wednesday morning has flooded many parts of Lagos

reports.impacts: About nine hours of non-stop rainfall from early Wednesday, plus daily rain the previous week that raised the Lagos lagoon. Flash floods inundated Iyana-Oworo linking Third Mainland and other areas. EFAG deployed; Iyana-Oworo cleared of blockages. Residents in low-lying areas told to relocate to higher ground.
reports.quote: Lagos has experienced about nine hours of non-stop rainfall since the early hours of Wednesday.
reports.cause_quote: heavy rainfall which the state has been experiencing daily since the previous week resulting in the rise in level of the Lagos lagoon
reports.cause_who: Tokunbo Wahab, Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources

reports.impacts: Flash flood from incessant early-Wednesday rain statewide. Nine hours of non-stop rain and a risen lagoon. Iyana Oworo linking Third Mainland inundated; EFAG cleared blockages there. Low-lying residents urged to move to higher ground; do not drive through floods.
reports.quote: the flash floods which inundated areas like Iyana Oworo linking the Third Mainland and several other areas
reports.cause_quote: heavy rainfall which the state has been experiencing on a daily basis since last week, resulting in the level rise of the Lagos lagoon
reports.cause_who: Tokunbo Wahab, Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources

reports.impacts: Business grounded after a 10-hour downpour Wednesday. Roads and houses flooded. Two-storey building on Cameroon Road, Ewenla, Mushin collapsed; seven rescued alive (three females, four males), none under rubble. White Sand Estate homes flooded to mid-level; school closed. Traffic fares Ogba–Ikeja rose from N300 to N700. Miscreants charged N100 at Trade Fair under-bridge; arrested.
reports.quote: Business and commercial activities were grounded on Wednesday following a 10-hour downpour in many parts of Lagos and Ogun states.
reports.cause_quote: Lagos experienced about nine hours of non-stop rainfall since the early hours of Wednesday
reports.cause_who: Tokunbo Wahab, Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources

reports.impacts: Early-morning rain paralysed most of the state; motorists trapped including on Third Mainland Bridge. Iyana-Oworo/Olopo Meji submerged; traffic to Alapere and old Toll Gate. Trees fell; roofs blown. Children kept from school. Hoodlums charged N100–N200 to carry pedestrians. LAWMA/Itire-Ikate LCDA locked a building after occupants dumped waste into street water.
reports.quote: activities in most parts of the state were paralysed following early morning rains that left many neighbourhoods heavily flooded
reports.cause_quote: The poor drainage network is worsened by the habit of dumping refuse in drainage channels which become blocked

reports.impacts: More than 10 hours of rain; flood into homes of Lekki, Ikoyi and Ajah. Residents fled to hotels. Mrs Shade: lost TV, fridge, furniture, mattress in a N3.5m/year two-bedroom. Correspondent saw three half-submerged cars; residents reported reptiles in water. Ajah: canoes on streets; markets abandoned; schools and businesses closed. Kunle Adesina: Olopomeji paths blocked by refuse were cleared and later returned to normal.
reports.quote: Streets became streams. Reptiles came out to play in the floodwater that overflowed roads and seeped into the homes of the rich
reports.cause_quote: the magnitude of rain is so much on the Island which is discharged into the Lagoon, the water level of the Lagoon rises
reports.cause_who: Kunle Adesina, Director of Public Affairs, Ministry of Environment and Water Resources

reports.impacts: Rain from about 3:00am Wednesday. Seven people rescued from a collapsed two-storey building at No 12 Cameroun Street, Mushin, after a 9:37am call; three females and four males taken to hospital; no one under rubble. Taiwo Ajisafe, Iyana-Oworo, could not go to work; house flooding. Over four hours Alapere to Third Mainland. Mary-Jane Ukeme, Ipaja: house under water in two hours; car fuel tank mixed with floodwater; ₦150,000 repair and ₦35,000 fuel lost.
reports.quote: Iyana-Oworo, Olopo Meji areas wey be di main entry point for 3rd mainland bridge bin dey seriously flooded
reports.cause_quote: one heavy rainfall wey bin start around early mor-mor 3:00am on Wednesday wey cause gbege across di state

reports.impacts: Early-Thursday downpour flooded major roads; commuters and motorists stranded. Oduche Azih, Okota: compound ankle- to knee-deep; flood seeped through walls into lower-level living room; blamed blockage of over one kilometre of drain ending at communal-effort bridge at Fasheun Drive. Traffic Alapere to Third Mainland. Some motorists parked because water volume could damage engines.
reports.quote: A downpour in the early hours of Thursday, caused widespread flooding in several parts of Lagos State, leaving commuters and motorists stranded.
reports.cause_quote: his Okota area was huge and caused by the total blockage of over one kilometre terminating at the communal effort bridge at Fasheun Drive

reports.impacts: Tuesday-morning downpour after months of heatwaves. Major roads submerged; residents stranded in apartments and cars. NEMA SW coordinator Ibrahim Farinloye: no life lost, no one injured. Houses: Oke Ishagun 23 evacuated; Isale Aboru 35 affected; Ikola 29; Olubodun Majiyagbe-Ajayi 15; Makinde Street 12; Olokowo Street 16; Adeola Street 21. Also mentioned a similar Sunday event.
reports.quote: Scores of houses were affected as downpour and flood hit Lagos State on Tuesday morning.
reports.cause_quote: In view of today’s excessive rainfall and the Sunday’s similar event
reports.cause_who: Ibrahim Farinloye, South West Coordinator, NEMA

reports.impacts: About 151 houses in Alimosho submerged. NEMA, Fire Service and Police rescued people trapped. No life lost, no one injured; many displaced. Ajasa Command Bridge overrun; residents told to use alternative routes. Flood later receding; Command Bridge still submerged at the visit.
reports.quote: About 151 houses within the Alimosho Local Government Area of Lagos were submerged in floods following excessive rainfall.
reports.cause_quote: About 151 houses within the Alimosho Local Government Area of Lagos were submerged in floods following excessive rainfall.

reports.impacts: Tuesday downpour hit Command and Ipaja; about 151 houses. Same NEMA house counts as Channels/Vanguard. No casualties or injuries. NEMA DG Mustapha Habib Ahmed appealed for drain clearing and prosecution of dumpers.
reports.quote: On Tuesday, Command and Ipaja communities in Lagos bore the brunt of the heavy downpour, witnessing the impact on approximately 151 houses
reports.cause_quote: the excessive rainfall on Tuesday, coupled with a downpour earlier in the week
reports.cause_who: Ibrahim Farinloye, Lagos Territorial Coordinator, NEMA

reports.impacts: Official inspection Thursday 27 June after flooding from 48 hours of continuous rain. EFAG deployed during the rain to clear collector debris. Encroachment/blockage behind James Hope University on Alfa Beach; excavation from Alpha Beach to Conservation Road to start Saturday. New collector planned on Agungi Road into the lagoon.
reports.quote: following the flooding incidents experienced as a result of the 48hrs continous rainfall experienced in the state
reports.cause_quote: the collector they have there is too small to Serve the volume of Storm water on the Agungi Streach
reports.cause_who: Tokunbo Wahab, Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources
reports.publisher: Lagos State Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources

reports.impacts: Rain from around 3 am Wednesday stranded thousands. Major roads and Third Mainland Bridge approaches flooded. Cars submerged; houses flooded. Wahab: Olopo Meji flash flood from high-intensity, long-duration rain plus high tidal lagoon level, expected to go in about 1–2 hours; EFAG cleared Alapomeji section of Iyana Oworo.
reports.quote: Thousands of commuters and motorists in Lagos state were stranded due to severe flooding of major roads
reports.cause_quote: a flash flood that is due to the high intensity of the rain, long duration rain coupled with high tidal lagoon level
reports.cause_who: Tokunbo Wahab, Commissioner for Environment and Water Resources
